title: EFX Existence — Two Agents, Any Finite Good Set
body_html:
EFX Existence — Two Agents, Any Finite Good Set

Theorem. For any two agents and any finite good set $G$, with an arbitrary monotone valuation $v$, there exists an EFX allocation ([[social_choice.fair_division.indivisible.efx]]).

In Lean: SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.efx_exists_two_agents. Hypotheses: [Fintype G], [DecidableEq G], valuation monotonicity.
proof_html:
outline

The standard "cut-and-choose"-style construction:

  1. Maximin enumeration. Enumerate all partitions of allGoods into two bundles. Pick the partition $(S, T)$ that maximizes the minimum of agent 0's values for the two halves, breaking ties leximin-style.

  2. Cut. This gives a partition where agent 0 is indifferent between $S$ and $T$ up to "removing-any-one-item" perturbations.

  3. Choose. Agent 1 picks their preferred half; agent 0 receives the other.

  4. EFX verification. The construction gives:

  5. Agent 0 is EFX by the maximin-leximin choice combined with monotonicity — any single-item perturbation cannot improve agent 0's worst-piece value, so removing any item from agent 1's bundle keeps it bounded by agent 0's own bundle value.
  6. Agent 1 is EFX trivially: they chose the strictly preferred side; removing any item from agent 0's bundle only decreases its value (by monotonicity), so agent 1 still prefers their own.

The Lean proof factors out mkAlloc_isAllocation, feasible_nonempty, optimal_exists for the partition-enumeration argument, then agent0_efx and agent1_efx close the two EFX directions separately.

Status of the wider EFX problem

Agent count EFX existence
$n = 2$ ✅ (this theorem)
$n = 3$ ✅ (Chaudhury–Garg–Mehlhorn 2020, not formalised here)
$n \ge 4$ 🔓 open

The 2-agent existence is the only case the library proves in full generality; the 3-agent case is on the porting roadmap but not yet formalised.

References

  • [AGT Chapter 11] Nisan, Roughgarden, Tardos, and Vazirani, Algorithmic Game Theory, references/AlgorithmicGameTheory.pdf. EFX existence for two agents.
  • Plaut, B. and Roughgarden, T. (2018). "Almost Envy-Freeness with General Valuations". SODA. arXiv:1707.04769.
  • Chaudhury, B. R., Garg, J., and Mehlhorn, K. (2020). "EFX Allocations for Three Agents". EC. arXiv:2005.06878.
